 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Toronto Raptors announced Tuesday that Kawhi Leonard will miss at least another week while he recovers from swelling in his left knee, ESPN reported . The team described him as "continuing the reconditioning process," which means he'll miss a minimum of three more games.
 He hasn't played since Oct. 23.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Leonard played in Toronto's first two games and averaged 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals, ESPN said . Then the swelling showed up. He was scratched about an hour before a 117-94 loss at Minnesota on Oct. 25 . An MRI showed no structural damage, but he has now missed eight games.
 ALSO READ: Trail Blazers aren't scared of anybody, and the Thunder felt it 
 Bleacher Report noted that the Raptors said last week that he had finished treatment and was starting the return-to-play process. Tuesday's update suggests that plan has slowed. Josh Lewenberg of TSN reported Leonard hadn't progressed to on-court work as of Tuesday, per the same piece.
 Head coach Darko Rajakovic said Sunday that Leonard had rejoined the team and was making good progress, according to Basketnews .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Toronto is leaning on a thin supporting cast 
 The Raptors are 5-5, and the margin for error is shrinking. Ja'Kobe Walter has taken Leonard's place in the starting lineup and is averaging 11.6 points. Jamal Shead is carrying more of the playmaking load, CBC Sports reported .
 The Toronto Raptors announced Tuesday that Kawhi Leonard will miss at least another week while he recovers from swelling in his left kneeStephen Gosling / Getty Images
 Leonard isn't the only name on the injury report. Scottie Barnes is out with a left groin strain, according to the NBA's report , and CBC said Immanuel Quickley is dealing with right hamstring soreness. Both could be out longer than the next game.
 The Celtics visit Toronto on Wednesday night, ClutchPoints reported , after beating Philadelphia 123-101 on Tuesday behind a 36-point night from Paul George . Boston is on the second half of a back-to-back, but the Raptors will be missing three of their most important players. That's a tough ask for a team trying to stay in the East race.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Toronto has a big contract and a long road to manage 
 Leonard is 35, and ESPN noted his history of right knee trouble, including multiple surgeries on his meniscus and ACL. The Raptors acquired him from the Clippers this offseason after what ESPN called a scandal-marred ending to his time in Los Angeles. He then agreed to a two-year, $115 million extension.
 That money gives Toronto every reason to move slowly. The next update is expected around Nov. 17. If Leonard hasn't reached on-court work by then, the Raptors may have to prepare for a much longer wait.
